name: La Voile - La Reserve Ramatuelle
recognition: Two MICHELIN stars since January 2020, held in the MICHELIN Guide France 2026; tourist-office listings also give three Gault&Millau toques (Gault&Millau's own pages split 15.5/20 vs 14/20).
what_to_order: Rouget poached in seawater|Beetroot cooked in seawater|All-vegetable tasting menu|Line-caught fish of the day
price_range: Gault&Millau gives EUR 195–350 per person before drinks (seen Oct 2026)
reservation: Book well ahead for the 2027 season; info@lareserve-ramatuelle.com
notes: Whatever garden-and-day-boat course is running, the crudites and vegetable plates, then a line-caught fish; Canino built his name on making a tomato or a courgette taste like the whole coastline.
verdict: This is the most decorated kitchen on the Saint-Tropez peninsula and it earns the fireworks by subtraction rather than excess, cooking in the wellness lineage that shaped it. Falsifiable claim: La Voile holds two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide France.
caveat: Price and booking: hotel-restaurant, menu-led prices well into three figures; dinner reservations essential and summer books solid. It closes out of season, so a winter visit finds it dark.

name: La Palmeraie — Château de Valmer
address: Château de Valmer, 81 boulevard de Gigaro, 83420 La Croix-Valmer, France
recognition: One MICHELIN star, 2026 (Relais & Châteaux listing); Gault&Millau two toques (2025, tourist listings).
what_to_order: Les meilleurs légumes de notre potager|Vegetarian set menu|Château de Valmer rosé
notes: "Les meilleurs légumes de notre potager" — the estate's just-picked vegetables read three ways on one plate: cooked but still crisp, in purée, and raw. The garden, not a protein, is the headline.
verdict: A one-star Relais & Châteaux dining room under a grove of century-old palms above Gigaro, cooking three Provençal set menus — one entirely vegetarian — around the vegetables, herbs and flowers of the estate's organic kitchen garden. One star in 2026, and open only for the summer season; who signs the menus is disputed between the sources (see the chef line).
caveat: Not a casual drop-in, and not in Cavalaire itself — it sits above Gigaro in La Croix-Valmer, opens only 8 May–4 October (2026), serves set menus at destination prices, and fills fast. Book well ahead; there is no walk-in stretch of the season.

name: Vista — Lily of the Valley
address: Lily of the Valley, Colline Saint-Michel, Bd Abel Faivre, Quartier de Gigaro (Plage de Gigaro), 83420 La Croix-Valmer, France
recognition: Gault&Millau 2026: 13/20, 'Table de Chef', chef Vincent Maillard. The hotel holds two MICHELIN Keys; no star for the restaurant.
what_to_order: Sisteron lamb shoulder braised with savory|Chickpea fries|Broccoli guacamole|Fisherman's catch|Champagne or Provence rosé
notes: Sisteron lamb shoulder braised with savory (sarriette), served to share (€98, seen Jul 2026) — the dish Gault&Millau singles out.
verdict: Order the Sisteron lamb shoulder braised with savory (€98, to share) and you'll taste why Gault&Millau gives it 13/20 (2026); à la carte runs roughly €25–150 a plate at a five-star hotel table with a sea-facing terrace — not a Michelin star it doesn't hold.
caveat: A five-star hotel dining room, not a hidden bistro: à la carte ran roughly €25–150 a plate (seen Jul 2026), and the room holds about 120 covers between the hall and its sea-facing terrace, so the draw is the cooking and the view, not intimacy. No MICHELIN star; a MICHELIN selection entry for the restaurant could not be confirmed (the hotel holds two MICHELIN Keys). Seasonal: its 2026 dates were not published — call before you plan on it.

name: Les Saisonniers
address: Boulevard de Tahiti (Les Palmiers II), 83420 La Croix-Valmer — in the village, above the municipal pool
tier: THE BERTHS · OUT OF THE PALACE KITCHENS — TWO CHEFS' ROOMS
recognition: Listed in the MICHELIN Guide (selection, no star or Bib); also recommended by Gault&Millau. 2026 edition not confirmed in an extract.
what_to_order: Pumpkin tartlet with goat-cheese ice cream|Squid stuffed with ratatouille|Marinated sea bream|Gnocchi with smoked ricotta|Cherry clafoutis
reservation: Book by phone or the restaurant directly; no online booking through MICHELIN
notes: Fine pumpkin tartlet with goat-cheese ice cream (and the squid stuffed with ratatouille) — the pastry-trained hand shows in both.
verdict: Three-star-trained pastry precision at village-bistro prices (~€45-60 a head), on a short, market-driven carte that turns with the season. Order the pumpkin tartlet under goat-cheese ice cream or the ratatouille-stuffed squid. Wrong choice only if you need a sea view or a table open all week.
caveat: The carte is short and rotates with the season, so the pumpkin tartlet or the ratatouille squid may not be on the day you go. It's a village room above the municipal pool, not a seafront table; the draw is the cooking, not a horizon. Opening days are limited — roughly Wed-Sat, lunch and dinner, plus a weekend brunch — and sources split on whether it opened February or March 2024.

name: Le Parc — L'Hôtel du Parc
address: Call ahead: tourist listing gives 7 avenue du Fleuriste; the hotel listing gives 8041 avenue des Orangers, 83240 Cavalaire-sur-Mer
tier: OUT OF THE PALACE KITCHENS — TWO CHEFS' ROOMS
recognition: Listed by Gault&Millau (page © 2025, marked sponsored), no toque or /20 score; no MICHELIN listing.
what_to_order: Label Rouge pork, artichokes and phô broth|Pêche du jour|Coquelet|Apricot three ways
notes: Label Rouge pork with artichokes and phô broth — the dish Gault&Millau flags first as the signature; the pêche du jour (daily catch) carries the fish billing.
verdict: In a town with no Michelin table, this is the one credible sit-down. Chef Jean-Brice Ruffroy, a veteran of starred kitchens, runs a bistronomic carte off named Provençal produce — Provence asparagus, Sisteron lamb, Perthuis potatoes — and the pêche du jour, served in the dining room or on the terrace over the park. Falsifiable: if you sit down and the menu isn't built on that named local sourcing plus a daily catch, this card is wrong.
caveat: The signal is a selection and a phrase, not a rating: Gault&Millau lists it with no toque and no /20 score published, and there is no Michelin nod — a resort town this size barely registers with the guides (Michelin: zero starred tables in Cavalaire). Naming is muddled too (the room reads as 'Le Parc'; the dinner service is branded 'La Table du Parc'). And note the honest mismatch: the guide-flagged marquee dishes are actually meat and fruit (Label Rouge pork, coquelet, apricot three ways) despite the fish-forward billing. It's a 4-star hotel restaurant — evening-focused, not a cheap eat — and seasonal: the dining room runs roughly late April to early October (closed Mondays), while in winter the chef and brigade decamp to Avoriaz.

name: La Pinède Plage
address: 382 Boulevard de Gigaro, 83420 La Croix-Valmer, France
tier: ON THE SAND — GIGARO AND THE GRANDE PLAGE
recognition: Gault&Millau 12/20, one toque, Table Gourmande (2025 review; no 2026 review found).
what_to_order: Octopus carpaccio|Tuna niçoise|Shellfish linguine|Burger de la Pinède
notes: Octopus cooked in court-bouillon, served carpaccio-style with a lemon-confit condiment, capers, tomato, rocket and pine nuts (the dish Gault&Millau leads its review with); the house "burger de la Pinède" is the casual counterpoint on the same card.
verdict: The most credible feet-near-the-sand table on Gigaro. A pine-shaded terrace facing the Îles d'Or where the octopus arrives cooked in court-bouillon, dressed as a carpaccio under a lemon-confit condiment with capers, tomato, rocket and pine nuts, alongside a tuna niçoise and shellfish linguine. Be clear about what it is: not a gastronomic temple. Gault&Millau gives it one toque and 12/20 — the mark of a very good beach kitchen, not a great restaurant. But on a shore where most tables coast on the view alone, this one actually cooks, and cooks with produce from the Château de Valmer's own kitchen garden.
caveat: This is the restaurant of a 4-star hotel's private beach: resort pricing, a yacht-stopover crowd (Gault&Millau notes it accommodates "yachtsmen on stopover"), and a short season — it runs only 30 April to 10 October (2026 dates confirmed), shut the rest of the year. One honest note on the signal: Gault&Millau's live page dates the 12/20 / one-toque rating to 2025, not 2026, so it is the current guide's score but carries a 2025 stamp. The executive menu is Thomas Pézéril's; the hotel's own site names Massimiliano d'Amico as the chef executing it day to day.

name: Marius à la plage
address: Plage de Gigaro, 83420 La Croix-Valmer (Golfe de Saint-Tropez, near Cavalaire-sur-Mer)
tier: ON THE SAND — GIGARO AND THE GRANDE PLAGE
product_tags: Beach restaurant, pieds dans l'eau (contemporary Provençal + grilled fish)
recognition: Run by Arthur and Sarah on Gigaro beach since April 2012; no MICHELIN or Gault&Millau listing.
what_to_order: Calamars grillés|Sardines grillées de Méditerranée|Tartare de bar|Douceur du Père Marius
notes: Calamars grillés — grilled squid with sauce vierge and homemade ratatouille (EUR 28); the sardines grillées de Méditerranée with ratatouille (EUR 24) run the same grilled-fish line. The house dessert "Douceur du Père Marius" (EUR 12) nods directly to the grandfather the place is named for.
verdict: The tables sit literally on the sand in the preserved bay at the far end of Gigaro, feet from the turquoise. Contemporary Provençal cooking built on freshly caught, grilled Mediterranean fish; in high summer, live musical apéritifs often run around 7–9pm. Run by Arthur and Sarah since April 2012.
caveat: No Michelin or Gault&Millau listing, and no critics' review surfaced in verification — this earns its place on genuine local reputation, not a guide badge. And you pay for the sand-and-sea setting: a tartare de bar main runs about EUR 49, grilled fish around EUR 24–28. Seasonal — open roughly early April (around 6 April) to the end of September; music times shift by night, so call ahead (04 94 54 25 05).

name: Tamaris Beach
address: Promenade de la Mer, 83240 Cavalaire-sur-Mer, France
tier: ON THE SAND — GIGARO AND THE GRANDE PLAGE
recognition: A private-beach lunch table on Cavalaire's Grande Plage; named in Little Weekends' Cavalaire guide (undated). No MICHELIN or Gault&Millau listing.
what_to_order: Poisson local à la plancha|Plat du jour|Fresh salads
price_range: Two loungers and a parasol about EUR 42 a day, lunch about EUR 25 (spiagge.it, undated; seen Oct 2026)
notes: Poisson local grille a la plancha — locally caught fish on the plancha, the anchor of a short card of salads and grilled meats and fish.
verdict: Come for a feet-in-the-sand lunch under the straw tonnelle on Cavalaire's main beach: a salad or a plancha-grilled local fish, water lapping a few metres away, open daily in season from 9h (closing between 18h and 20h depending on the source). It's an honest beach table, not a kitchen with ambition — arrive expecting gastronomy and you'll be let down; the fish and the sand are the whole point.
caveat: No Michelin or Gault&Millau listing, and none should be expected — this is a plage-privee lunch spot, not a gastronomic address. Seasonal only (published dates 30 March to 5 November); a day package of two loungers and a parasol runs about EUR 42 and a midday meal about EUR 25, so it's a beach-club sit-down, not cheap eats. No owner or chef is named in any source.
hot_this_month: Last lunches on the sand: listed open until 5 November 2026, plancha fish under the straw tonnelle; phone before going (checked 21 Oct 2026).

name: Le Comptoir des Saveurs
address: Nouveau Port, 83240 Cavalaire-sur-Mer, Var, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
tier: FISH BY THE WATER — THE PORT, THE CLIFF, THE PINES
recognition: Owner-run Provençal and fish restaurant on the Nouveau Port, listed by the Golfe de Saint-Tropez tourist office; no Michelin or Gault&Millau entry
what_to_order: Aïoli provençal complet|Daube de joue de bœuf|Pissaladière|Moules
notes: Aïoli provençal complet (~€29.50, per aggregated listings) — salt cod and boiled vegetables under a garlic-heavy sauce; the daube de joue de bœuf braised in red wine and the pissaladière are the supporting emblems the kitchen leans on, all three named on the restaurant's own site and the regional tourism board.
verdict: Order the traditional aïoli (aggregated listings put the formula around €29.50): salt cod, boiled seasonal vegetables and a thick, garlic-forward sauce — the real Provençal ritual, not a decorative version. Get that plate right, plus a pissaladière and the red-wine daube of beef cheek, and this is honest port cooking. If the aïoli comes garlic-shy and under-seasoned, or the pissaladière tastes sweet and jarred, this card is wrong.
caveat: No guide backs this; it rests on local standing and review sites. The tourist listing gives a March–October season, the old record said February–October: in late October call before walking down. Closed days per the house site (Wednesday off, dinner only Monday, Tuesday and Thursday) were not rechecked. Aggregated reviews include complaints about fish served raw and about service; the aïoli formula is the value play.

name: Le Grand Bleu — Hôtel de la Calanque
address: 20 rue (or avenue) de la Calanque, 83240 Cavalaire-sur-Mer
tier: FISH BY THE WATER — THE PORT, THE CLIFF, THE PINES
recognition: Hotel restaurant on the cliff above the Cron cove; Gault&Millau directory entry without a score; member of the Collège Culinaire de France since 2024
what_to_order: Bouillabaisse de la calanque|Risotto au homard|Linguine with cuttlefish and parsley
notes: The bouillabaisse de la calanque with its aïoli and a lobster risotto were the house plates in July 2026; neither shows on the 2026 menus seen in October, where reviews point to the cuttlefish linguine — ask what is on.
verdict: A view-first fish house on a terrace pinned to the cliff above the Cron cove, east of Cavalaire's port: come for the drop to the sea and the day's fish. What it is not: a critics' address. No MICHELIN listing; Gault&Millau carries a directory entry without a toque or a score (seen Jul 2026). It is a member of the chef-founded Collège Culinaire de France (since 2024) — peer recognition, not a critic's ranking.
caveat: Hours drift by source and season — this is a seasonal Riviera hotel-restaurant, so confirm it's open before you go. Little Weekends lists dinner daily plus weekend lunches; the hotel's own page lists lunch daily (12:00–17:00) and dinner Tuesday–Sunday (19:00–21:30); Gault&Millau shows yet another weekly pattern. The reputation is built on the setting first: per Little Weekends, entrées 18–24€, plats 28–36€, desserts 15€. Come for the terrace and the calanque, not for a critical pedigree that doesn't exist.

name: Le Refuge
address: 1412 Boulevard de Gigaro, 83420 La Croix-Valmer (Gigaro), near Cavalaire-sur-Mer
tier: FISH BY THE WATER — THE PORT, THE CLIFF, THE PINES
recognition: Seaside restaurant under the pines of Gigaro, founded 1964, reopened 2019; no Michelin or Gault&Millau ranking
what_to_order: Assiette du pêcheur|Confit Sisteron lamb shoulder|Tapas on the terrace
price_range: EUR 30–60 or 40–80 depending on the listing (seen Oct 2026)
notes: No single fixed signature — the card changes week to week with the season. Cooking leans on local produce and, per the house, "traditional fishermen"; the standing seafood option is The Fisherman's Plate (assiette du pecheur, ~38 euros), set alongside land plates like confit Sisteron lamb shoulder and a roasted Bresse-style poultry dish, so the sea is only ever part of the story.
verdict: Come for a produce-led lunch on the broad sea-view terrace over Gigaro bay: the card reads to the season and leans on the local catch and Mediterranean produce, not a printed year-round list. If it turns up as a fixed tourist menu of frozen fish, the whole reason to choose it over the neighbouring beach spots is gone.
caveat: No Michelin or Gault&Millau ranking, and no press feature surfaced — it earns its place on local standing and a seasonal, produce-led kitchen, not a guide score. It is seaside, not a working quay: a terrace among Gigaro's centenary parasol pines overlooking the bay (Petit Fute lists it as a "restaurant de plage"). Seasonal operation — the 2026 season ran roughly 7 Mar to 31 Oct — though the house site confusingly also says "open all year." Chef attribution is unsettled: the current site credits Laurent Latreille while 2025 tourism listings still name Sebastien Massart (weekly-changing menu), so a recent handover is likely; neither is independently confirmed, so no chef is asserted here. Founded 1964, reopened 2019 after a long renovation. Coordinates are approximate.
hot_this_month: On its autumn timetable until 31 October 2026: lunch and dinner Monday, Thursday, Friday and weekends, closed Tuesday and Wednesday (checked 21 Oct 2026).

name: Maurin des Maures
tier: THE BERTHS · ALONG THE CORNICHE DES MAURES
recognition: Gilles Pudlowski, 'Rayol-Canadel : Dédé l'éternel', Les Pieds dans le Plat (Sept 2025), after 'Au bonheur de Dédé' (July 2022); Gault&Millau 11/20 in the old record
what_to_order: Bouillabaisse du pêcheur|Terrine de bouillabaisse|Menu du jour
price_range: Menu du jour EUR 22.50; à la carte EUR 55–75 (Pudlowski, Sept 2025); bouillabaisse about EUR 85.50 per person, minimum two (seen 2026)
reservation: Phone the day before for the bouillabaisse
notes: Bouillabaisse du pêcheur, served for at least two people, à commander la veille (chapon, congre, saint-pierre, grondin, vive, crabe, moules, safran, huile d'olive) — €76.50 for a pot serving two, per Pudlowski, 2022.
verdict: The bouillabaisse Pudlowski calls a monument: a two-person cauldron of chapon, congre, saint-pierre, grondin, vive, crabe and moules that you must phone in the day before. Skip that call and there's little reason to make the drive down to the cove.
caveat: Order the bouillabaisse the day before — Pudlowski's exact phrase is "à commander la veille", not the "48h" sometimes quoted. Treat €76.50 for a pot serving two as Pudlowski's 2022 figure: the current menu lists the bouillabaisse du pêcheur at around €85.50 a person, two people minimum (seen Jul 2026). A splurge plate, not a cheap eat. No current Guide du Routard listing was found: the signal rests on Pudlowski and Gault&Millau (11/20). One listing says no dinner from 11 November to 20 December: call.

name: Le Café des Jardiniers — Domaine du Rayol
address: Domaine du Rayol – Le Jardin des Méditerranées, Avenue Jacques Chirac (ex-Avenue des Belges), 83820 Rayol-Canadel-sur-Mer, Var
recognition: Café-restaurant inside the Conservatoire du littoral's Domaine du Rayol, garden by Gilles Clément; chef Tom Ortin; covered by Pudlowski (Sept 2025)
what_to_order: Souris d'agneau au jus de thym du jardin|Winter vegetable velouté|Daily vegetarian plate|Homemade ice creams
notes: Souris d'agneau au jus de thym du jardin — lamb shank in a jus of thyme cut from the garden, with grenaille potatoes and roasted vegetables. Directly attested as an official menu example, but it is part of a daily-rotating chalkboard, so not guaranteed on any given day.
verdict: The one lunch on this coast you reach by walking through a botanical garden of the world's Mediterranean climates. On a terrace in the heart of the Domaine du Rayol, chef Tom Ortin cooks a short, seasonal Provençal chalkboard — everything made on-site, a vegetarian plate every day, homemade ice creams. Falsifiable and verified: it exists only for people who have paid garden admission, takes no reservations (except groups of 15+), and the kitchen serves lunch only, 12:00–14:30, even though the café/tea-room runs from about 10:30 until an hour before the garden closes. Open year-round, seven days, except 25 December.
caveat: This is a garden-and-a-plate outing, not a restaurant you can just book. You cannot eat here without buying a Domaine du Rayol garden ticket, and it seats garden visitors only — the ticket does not guarantee a table. No reservations except groups of 15+; at busy times it's a wait-list on site. The kitchen is lunch-only (12:00–14:30); outside that the terrace serves drinks, a gourmet break and ice cream, not full plates. The "nougat" ice cream flavour and the "Little Weekends" guide mention could not be verified and have been dropped — homemade/artisanal ice creams are confirmed, but the specific flavour rotates.
hot_this_month: The Domaine du Rayol garden is open every day on winter hours; a gardener-led walk runs on 20 November 2026; check the café is serving lunch before you plan on it (checked 21 Oct 2026).

name: Bello Visto
address: Place deis Barri, old village, 83580 Gassin
tier: THE HILL VILLAGES — GASSIN AND RAMATUELLE
recognition: In the MICHELIN Guide selection (€€€, traditional cuisine; no Bib Gourmand shown); Gault&Millau 13/20, Table de Chef
what_to_order: Cassolette de poulpe de roche|Gnocchi à la truffe|Soufflé au Grand Marnier|Suggestion du jour
price_range: EUR 43–65 per person before drinks (Gault&Millau); MICHELIN price band €€€ (seen Oct 2026)
reservation: Book and ask for the rampart terrace
notes: The seasonal Provencal mains and the day's fish and octopus preparations; ask for the day's suggestion and sit on the rampart terrace at sunset, not inside.
verdict: Come for traditional Provençal cooking with the gulf laid out below the ramparts: the octopus casserole, the truffle gnocchi and the Grand Marnier soufflé are the plates MICHELIN names. Falsifiable claim: it is in the MICHELIN selection as a €€€ traditional table and Gault&Millau scores it 13/20, Table de Chef, about EUR 43–65 a head; it is not a Bib Gourmand, whatever older lists say.
caveat: Booking: the famous view means the terrace tables are fought over, so reserve and request outside. It is a small village hotel-restaurant, not a scene, which is exactly the appeal.

name: La Verdoyante
tier: THE HILL VILLAGES — GASSIN AND RAMATUELLE
recognition: Mouret family restaurant over the Gassin vineyards; listed by Gault&Millau, Le Routard and Petit Futé (tourist office); MICHELIN 2026 not confirmed
reservation: Telephone only; full several days ahead from June to early October
notes: Whatever is built on the day's garden and herbs, the kitchen leans hard into thyme-and-rosemary garrigue flavours, plus classics like fish soup and bourride; the panoramic terrace over the domaines is the reason to book lunch.
verdict: The anti-Saint-Tropez table: no scene, no DJ, just southern home cooking on a wide terrace over the vines of Minuty, run by two generations of the Mouret family. Falsifiable claim: it is listed by Gault&Millau, Le Routard and Petit Futé and books out days ahead in high season; a MICHELIN listing could not be confirmed for 2026.
caveat: Seasonal (roughly spring to autumn) and it is out among the vineyards, so you need a car. Honesty by negation: comfort and setting over cutting-edge cooking.

name: La Forge
tier: THE HILL VILLAGES — GASSIN AND RAMATUELLE
recognition: Gault&Millau 13/20 (review labelled 2025); earlier praise from Gilles Pudlowski and Jacques Gantié
what_to_order: Fresh house pasta|Vitello tonnato|Osso buco|House bread
price_range: À la carte EUR 50–80 (tourist office); Gault&Millau about EUR 39 a head before drinks (seen Oct 2026)
notes: Fresh house-made pasta and bread and the day's Italian fish; the kitchen cooks regional Italy, so order whatever is most Italian and least generic Cote d'Azur.
verdict: Ramatuelle village's most convincing non-French table: a chef from Le Marche and a Piedmont-Lake-Maggiore host who cook Italy straight, from a panoramic terrace in an old forge. Falsifiable claim: it is run by chef Paolo Amadori and Francesca Alessi, both Italian-born, not a French 'trattoria' concept.
caveat: Price and booking: this is village-near-Saint-Tropez pricing and summer-busy, and the good terrace tables need reserving. Honest cooking, not a bargain.

name: The fishermen's stand, Quai Marc Pajot
neighborhood: Cavalaire · Vieux Port, Quai Marc Pajot
address: Quai Marc Pajot, Port de Cavalaire, 83240 Cavalaire-sur-Mer (by the fishermen's auction point)
tier: LA RUE — OFF THE BOAT, THE WEDNESDAY MARKET, THE PORT GLASS
recognition: Direct sale by Cavalaire's fishermen on Quai Marc Pajot, listed by the town and the regional tourism board
what_to_order: Rockfish for soupe de roche|Sea bream and sea bass|Red mullet|Langouste or spider crab
notes: Rockfish for soup; the day's bream, bass and red mullet.
verdict: Cavalaire keeps a small working fleet, and the boats sell straight off the quay most mornings from about 10:00, catch and weather permitting: girelle, rascasse and chapon for the soupe de roche, sea bream and sea bass, sometimes a spider crab or a langouste.
caveat: Weather and catch decide: some mornings there is nothing, and in winter the boats go out less. The town does not name the fishermen or say which days of the year the stall runs. Bring cash and a cool bag; payment methods not confirmed.
hot_this_month: Autumn mornings on the quay from about 10:00, weather and catch permitting: rockfish for the soupe de roche, the day's bream, bass and red mullet. Whether the stand works every winter morning is not confirmed: go and look.

name: Wednesday market, Place Jean Moulin
tier: THE BERTHS · LA RUE — OFF THE BOAT, THE WEDNESDAY MARKET, THE PORT GLASS
recognition: Provençal market, Place Jean Moulin, every Wednesday 08:30–13:00, all year
what_to_order: Tapenade and anchoïade|Pissaladière|Pan bagnat|Maures honey|Golfe de Saint-Tropez rosé
notes: Tapenade, anchoïade, honey of the Maures, the gulf's rosé.
verdict: Around a hundred stalls every Wednesday morning, year-round, roughly 08:30–13:00: tapenade and anchoïade, olives, honey and olive oil, cheese and charcuterie, fish and seasonal fruit, and the rosé of the gulf.
caveat: Morning only: it folds by one. Clothing, jewellery and craft stalls share the square with the food. The 'around a hundred stalls' count in the old guide was not confirmed.
hot_this_month: The Wednesday morning market carries on all winter; 11 November, Armistice Day, falls on a Wednesday, so check it is held that week (checked 21 Oct 2026).

name: Ô Petit Bar
address: 24 Résidence du Port, Rue du Port, 83240 Cavalaire-sur-Mer
tier: LA RUE — OFF THE BOAT, THE WEDNESDAY MARKET, THE PORT GLASS
recognition: Harbour cocktail bar; Little Weekends singles out its mojitos ('les meilleurs mojitos de la région'); no guide ranking
what_to_order: Mojito|Îles d'Or craft beer|Toasted cheese tartines
notes: The mojito — the house drink the travel blog Little Weekends calls "les meilleurs mojitos de la région." Everything else stays deliberately light: cocktails with or without alcohol, Îles d'Or craft beers, organic juices, and roasted-cheese/croque-style tartines.
verdict: Come for the drink, not the meal. This is a small, convivial port bar with a clear view over the Cavalaire marina where the pour — a mojito — is the point; the kitchen never leaves snack territory (roasted-cheese tartines, croque-style toasts, house pesto and tapenade). Falsifiable: turn up on an open evening and you'll find it pouring cocktails toward 1am with the harbour in front of you, not a plated dinner service — anyone arriving hungry for a proper meal will be disappointed.
caveat: Not a dining recommendation and carries no authority ranking — no Michelin, Gault&Millau, Routard or 50 Best entry exists for a port bar this small; the only cosign is a travel blog's "best mojitos" line, resting otherwise on genuine local port reputation, so treat "best in the region" as an enthusiast's pick, not a verdict. Hours are genuinely inconsistent across listings: Little Weekends says 18h–1h daily; the bar's own eatbu page says 17h–1h and closed Thursdays; other directories show a Wednesday closure, a ~00h30 close and a Sunday daytime-only window. Call ahead (+33 6 98 30 14 60) rather than trust one schedule, and don't count on the same closed day.
